tool.name: qiime2 sidle trim-dada2-posthoc
tool.description: Trim a dada2 ASV table and rep set to a consistent length.
tool.command: export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="\$PWD/xdgconfig" MPLCONFIGDIR="\$PWD/mplconfigdir" NUMBA_CACHE_DIR="\$PWD/numbacache" CONDA_PREFIX=/opt/conda/envs/sidle-0.1.0-beta && q2galaxy run sidle trim_dada2_posthoc '$inputs'

param.name: table
param.label: table: FeatureTable[Frequency]
param.help: [required] A feature table generated by a denoising algorithm with variable length ASVs.

param.name: representative_sequences
param.label: representative_sequences: FeatureData[Sequence]
param.help: [required] The corresponding representative sequences for the ASV table.

param.name: trim_length
param.label: trim_length: Int % Range(0, None)
param.help: [default: 0] The length ASVs should be trimmed to. If the trim length is 0, the shortest sequence will be used. Alternatively, if a trim length is specified which is longer than some of the sequences, those ASVs will be discarded.

param.name: hashed_feature_ids
param.label: hashed_feature_ids: Bool
param.help: [default: Yes] If true, the feature ids in the resulting table will be presented as hashes of the sequences defining each feature. The hash will always be the same for the same sequence so this allows feature tables to be merged across runs of this method. You should only merge tables if the exact same parameters are used for each run.

tool.help:
QIIME 2: sidle trim-dada2-posthoc ================================= Trim a dada2 ASV table and rep set to a consistent length.
Outputs: -------- :trimmed_table.qza: ASV table with consistent length ASVs. :trimmed_representative_sequences.qza: ASV sequences of a consistent length.
|
Description: ------------ This function trims ASVs generated by DADA2 to a consistent length and collapses them into a single sequence as appropriate. This is necessary to be able to use a DADA2 ASV table with the SMURF algorithm, which requires a consistent sequence length. NOTE: This should be done before anything else that requires ASV sequences because it may change ASV IDs.
|
